question: The elements which have 2 electrons in their outermost cell are generally:
solution:
The correct answer is __**metals**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Elements with 2 electrons in their outermost shell are generally **metals.**
 
• These elements are often found in the second group of the periodic table and are known as the **alkaline earth metals.**
 
• The common examples include **beryllium (Be), magnesium (Mg), calcium (Ca), strontium (Sr), barium (Ba), and radium (Ra).**
 
• Alkaline earth metals are characterized by their **shiny appearance and high reactivity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkaline earth metals** have an oxidation state of +2, which is why they readily lose two electrons to form cations.
 
• These metals are less reactive than alkali metals (group 1) but are still highly reactive, particularly with water and oxygen.
 
• Due to their reactivity, they are not found in their free elemental state in nature but are commonly found in various minerals.
 
• Their reactivity increases as you move down the group in the periodic table.
 
• These metals also have relatively low densities and low melting points compared to other metals.
